source.name: LiveBench (sub-categories)
source.description: LiveBench 2.0 per-subcategory scores (33 subcategories of the 7 suites), release 2026-11-06.
source.license: No license stated on the leaderboard data files; LiveBench GitHub repo is Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/LiveBench/LiveBench/blob/main/LICENSE). Site has no terms page (https://livebench.ai/terms -> 404) and robots.txt allows all (https://livebench.ai/robots.txt). Values are published results, reused with credit.
source.attribution: LiveBench (White et al., 'LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark', arXiv:2406.19314), https://livebench.ai
notes: Release used: 20261106 (2026-11-06), the latest release listed in the site's JS (releases 20261014, 20261025, 20261106).

Scores are copied directly from breakdown.json (<suite>.models.<model>.scores.<subcategory>); LiveBench publishes these values itself, no recomputation. The site shows them with toFixed(1) as columns and toFixed(0) in the expanded row.

Per the site: the suite score is computed over all its tasks, not as the mean of subcategory scores, so subcategory scores do not average to the suite score. Each cell is a mean task score 0-100 from a single run; a task the run could not measure scores 0. Some subcategories have very few tasks (2-5), so scores move in coarse steps.

Model names are the table.csv / breakdown.json model keys; developer, reasoning_effort, display_name, open_weight come from the site's model catalog in main.099aad9b.js. All 41 table.csv models are in the catalog (shown on the site).
No cost, time or token data per subcategory is published (cost.csv / llm_time.csv are per suite only).
model = LiveBench's display name (as in data/livebench.json); the table.csv key is kept in extra.table_key
